title: Proper to God alone; created 'necessaries' only secundum quid
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): But we assert that this absolute necessity belonging toward existing so proper unto God is that unto no creature can it be attributed. For although some created beings necessary are called, as spiritual substances plus heavenly bodies: yet not simply but in a certain respect so are they called; because naturally plus by ye force belonging toward natural causes they cannot be destroyed — which properly speaking to be incorruptible is.
pass_b_english: But we assert that this absolute necessity of existing is so proper to God that it can be attributed to no creature. For although some created beings are called necessary, as spiritual substances and heavenly bodies: yet they are so called not simply but in a certain respect; because they cannot be destroyed naturally and by the force of natural causes — which properly speaking is to be incorruptible.
source_text: Asserimus autem hanc absolutam exsistendi necessitatem ita propriam esse Deo, ut nulli creaturae attribui possit. Quamvis enim nonnulla entia creata dicantur necessaria, ut substantiae spirituales & corpora caelestia: ea tamen non simpliciter, sed secundum quid ita appellantur; quia naturaliter & vi causarum naturalium destrui nequeunt; id quod proprie loquendo est esse incorruptibile.
